desc:
Encoding. A singly linked list with n nodes is given by two arrays. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1; node 0 is the head, vals[i] is the value stored in node i and succ[i] is the number of the node after node i, or -1 if there is none. The node numbers say nothing about the order in the list: follow succ to find it.

The list has an even number n of nodes and no cycle. Number the nodes in list order 0..n-1 (position 0 is the head). The twin of the node at position i is the node at position n - 1 - i, so the first node is paired with the last, the second with the second to last, and so on. The twin sum of a pair is the sum of its two values.

Return the largest twin sum. Example: the list 4 -> 2 -> 2 -> 3 (vals = [4,2,2,3], succ = [1,2,3,-1]) has the pairs (4, 3) and (2, 2), with sums 7 and 4, so the answer is 7.

A solution with O(1) extra space exists: use only pointers, no array copy of the list.
constraints: The list starting at node 0 visits all n nodes and ends at a node with succ = -1
hints: Copying the values into an array and pairing index i with n - 1 - i solves it, but uses O(n) memory.
The second half of the list, read backwards, is exactly the list of twins of the first half, in order. How do you read a half backwards without extra memory?
Find the start of the second half with a slow and a fast pointer, reverse the second half in place, and then walk the first half and the reversed second half together, taking the maximum of the sums.
editorial: With a slow pointer (one step) and a fast pointer (two steps) started at the head, the slow pointer stands at position n/2, the first node of the second half, when the fast pointer runs off the end (n is even, so there is no middle node to worry about).

Reverse the part of the list that starts there. Its first node is now the original last node, the twin of the head. Walk one pointer from the head and one from that reversed half in lockstep: the two nodes at every step are twins, so the maximum of their value sums is the answer.
Each of the three phases is O(n) and only pointers are used, so the total is O(n) time and O(1) space (the reversal here is performed on a copy of succ only because the arrays are inputs).
solution:
def maxTwinSum(vals, succ):
    nxt = succ[:]
    slow = fast = 0
    while fast != -1 and nxt[fast] != -1:
        slow = nxt[slow]
        fast = nxt[nxt[fast]]
    prev, cur = -1, slow
    while cur != -1:
        after = nxt[cur]
        nxt[cur] = prev
        prev, cur = cur, after
    a, b = 0, prev
    best = None
    for _ in range(len(vals) // 2):
        s = vals[a] + vals[b]
        if best is None or s > best:
            best = s
        a = nxt[a]
        b = nxt[b]
    return best
